entry.label: Critical Systems Heuristics (CSH)
entry.description: Critical Systems Heuristics is a framework for examining the boundary judgements built into plans and interventions: who benefits, who decides, what counts as expertise, and who or what is left outside.

profile.title: Critical Systems Heuristics (CSH)
profile.canonical_definition: Critical Systems Heuristics is a framework for examining the boundary judgements built into plans and interventions: who benefits, who decides, what counts as expertise, and who or what is left outside.
profile.summary: Critical Systems Heuristics is a framework for reflective and critical practice which makes boundary judgements and their consequences discussable.
profile.why_it_matters: CSH provides a disciplined way to examine who benefits, who decides, what counts as knowledge and how those affected can challenge claims to improvement.
common_misreadings: the twelve questions are a checklist survey
only emancipatory projects can use CSH
profile.editorial_note: Developed from public primary, institutional and publisher sources. Open to correction, rival interpretation and stronger evidence.
